label: GO after a2 S2 rewarded, strongest when previous S1 trial was unrewarded; fades over episode
terms: (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (tv("state", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * ep_trial ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (tv("stay", -1) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == -1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (belief < 0.5) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (tv("reward", -2) == -9)
explanation: hidden/3 fires only at GO. Its magnitude is set by the last trial being a2 -> S2 rewarded (base weight ~+0.18), with a large boost (~+0.63) when the trial before that reached S1 and went unrewarded (fresh evidence that S2 is now good after an S1 loss). It decays with episode trial (~-0.003 per trial), is somewhat lower (~-0.16) when the a2 choice on the last trial was itself a switch, and is raised at window-first trials when the shown reward was 1 and the ideal-observer belief favours S2 (prev state unknown). Other previous-trial patterns give ~0 (negative residual vs timing). Graded belief_lo terms add little beyond the a2 S2 r indicator. Observed-only test R^2 beyond timing 0.467 (dev 0.467), above the profile all ceiling 0.41 and all-observed 0.35; the earlier value/policy-based firing account (value deciles 7-8, a2-leaning policy) is not needed for magnitude: trial history alone captures it.

issues: The core claims hold on the test split. a2 S2 r on the last trial alone gives R^2 0.143. Adding 'trial -2 unrewarded' raises it to 0.321, and splitting that by state gives S1 loss +0.585 vs S2 loss +0.12 (0.378), so 'strongest after a prior S1 loss' is correct.

The stay term is close to redundant: dropping it lowers test R^2 only from 0.467 to 0.464. It mostly stands in for which action was taken at trial -2. With a full table on the trial -2 pattern (given last = a2 S2 r), a2 S1 u gives +0.67, a1 S1 u +0.48, a2 S2 u +0.18 and every rewarded pattern about 0. So the 'switch lowers it' claim really means that losing after a2 matters more than losing after a1. It is not a separate switch effect.

The explanation leaves out that an S2 loss at trial -2 also boosts the feature (+0.18 after a2 S2 u). It also leaves out that the after-a-loss boost itself fades over the episode: adding L*ep_trial gives about +0.017 R^2.

The ep_trial fade is real: dropping it lowers test R^2 from 0.467 to 0.431. The window-first-trial term is also real (0.434 without it). A graded (1-belief) version does slightly better than the belief<0.5 cutoff (0.474).

Belief terms add nothing on the a2 S2 r rows (belief, tv('belief',-1), belief change: all +0.000 test). So the claim that observed trial history is enough, and that dropping value/policy loses nothing, is supported.

Misses: the largest remaining errors are at the window's first trial or where trial -2 falls outside the window (actual about 1.4-1.5 vs predicted 0.12-0.25). Those trials' history is not in the window, and belief does not recover it (the A*(reward-2==-9)*(1-belief) term got weight 0.007). This is a limit of the data, not a wrong label. The other errors by phase x previous trial are flat (about -0.045 for all GO non-a2S2r cells), i.e. an intercept effect, not a missing pattern.
